plan.goal: Which countries emitted the most CO2 in 2022, and how does that ranking change when emissions are measured per person rather than in total?
goal_candidates: Which countries have the highest CO2 emissions per person, and which of them are also the biggest total emitters?
How closely does a country's total CO2 output track the size of its population?
How unevenly is per-capita CO2 spread across the world's countries in 2022?
plan.understanding: This is a one-year (2022) cross-section of national CO2 emissions from the Global Carbon Project / Our World in Data style dataset, with 254 rows and one row per country or aggregate region. Each row gives a place's total CO2 emissions, its emissions per person, and its population. The country column deliberately mixes real countries (Afghanistan, New Zealand) with aggregates such as World, continents, income groups and GCP/OECD regions, and those aggregate rows are the ones whose iso_code is blank. The file is a single snapshot with no date column, so the report is a ranking/comparison rather than a trend.

columns.name: country
columns.why: the entity each row describes; it also holds aggregates (World, Africa, High-income countries, GCP regions) that must be removed

columns.name: iso_code
columns.why: 3-letter country code; blank on exactly the aggregate rows, so it is the cleanest filter for real countries

columns.name: co2
columns.why: total CO2 emitted in 2022; World total of ~37,500 matches this million-tonne scale

columns.name: co2_per_capita
columns.why: the intensity measure that separates small high-emitting states from large populous ones

columns.name: population
columns.why: country population, the natural scale factor behind total emissions; flagged as personal but clearly a country total

analyses.why: the top emitters by total and by per-person emissions are different sets of countries
shows how much of a country's total emissions is explained by its population size
most countries sit near a few tonnes per person while a handful of oil and gas states run far above

quality_risks: The country column mixes sovereign states with aggregates (World, continents, income groups, GCP/OECD regions); these have blank iso_code and would swamp any ranking if kept.
Emissions are missing for some rows (co2 blank on 7, co2_per_capita on 23, population on 25), so small or oil-producing states may drop out of per-capita comparisons.
Total co2 is in million tonnes while co2_per_capita is in tonnes per person; the two must never be plotted on one untransformed axis.
Total emissions are dominated by population size, so a ranking on co2 alone will just list the largest countries — the per-capita view is needed alongside it.
Some rows show co2 = 0, which is likely rounded-away tiny emissions rather than true zero, so the lowest values should not be read literally.
population carries a 'looks personal' flag, but it is a country-level total and is safe to use as a scale factor.
